proposals.before: Confucius said, “Human beings broadened the Way; it was never the Way that broadened human beings.”
proposals.after: Confucius said, “Human beings can broaden the Way; it is not the Way that broadens human beings.”
proposals.reason: The Chinese 能 marks present capacity (人能弘道); the idiomatic English drops “can” and uses past tense, which obscures the Analects sense preserved in the literal rendering.

proposals.before: Legend credits the Yellow Emperor with “Cloud Gate,” Yao with “Mulberry Pool,” Shun with “Grand Shao,” Yu with “Grand Xia,” Yin with “Grand Hu,” and Zhou with “Grand Wu”—music that continued older court ritual, choreographed every inclination of the body, hoarded gentle obedience inwardly, and let splendor shine outward.
proposals.after: Legend credits the Yellow Emperor with “Cloud Gate,” Yao with “Xianchi,” Shun with “Grand Shao,” Yu with “Grand Xia,” Yin with “Grand Hu,” and Zhou with “Grand Wu”—music that continued older court ritual, choreographed every inclination of the body, hoarded gentle obedience inwardly, and let splendor shine outward.
proposals.reason: 咸池 is the ritual piece Xianchi, not a mulberry pool; 桑 would be required for “mulberry.”

proposals.before: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor made “Cloud Gate”; Yao made “Mulberry Pool”; Shun made “Grand Shao”; Yu made “Grand Xia”; Yin made “Grand Hu”; Zhou made “Grand Wu”—what is called inheriting the former kings’ ritual, setting out gestures of bowing and rising, storing harmony and compliance within, and letting splendid brilliance burst forth without.
proposals.after: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor made “Cloud Gate”; Yao made “Xianchi”; Shun made “Grand Shao”; Yu made “Grand Xia”; Yin made “Grand Hu”; Zhou made “Grand Wu”—what is called inheriting the former kings’ ritual, setting out gestures of bowing and rising, storing harmony and compliance within, and letting splendid brilliance burst forth without.
proposals.reason: 咸池 is Xianchi; “Mulberry Pool” invents 桑 and mistranslates the music title.

proposals.before: When favor lavished on Bao Si invited disaster and King Ping’s reign dissolved in turmoil, ritual collapsed between close kin and remote branches, and instruments of music were drowned as if in flood tide.
proposals.after: When favor lavished on Bao Si invited disaster and King Ping met with turmoil, ritual collapsed between close kin and remote branches, and instruments of music were drowned as if in flood tide.
proposals.reason: 平王逢亂 means King Ping encountered disorder, not that his own reign dissolved in turmoil; 逢亂 is the meeting with chaos after Western Zhou’s collapse.

proposals.before: So when Prince Jizi of Yanling heard the “Lesser Elegantiae,” he declared, “This is Zhou virtue in decay.
proposals.after: So when Prince Jizi of Yanling heard the “Lesser Elegantiae,” he declared, “Is this Zhou virtue in decay?
proposals.reason: 其周德之衰乎 is a rhetorical question, which the literal rendering preserves; the idiomatic version turns it into a plain assertion.

proposals.before: Palace women repudiated Confucian doctrine and ministers spurned Jia Yi’s memorials—so belted scholars groaned aloud, even Liu Xiang and Dong Zhongshu struggling to hold their peace.
proposals.after: The empress dowager repudiated Confucian doctrine and ministers spurned Jia Yi’s memorials—so belted scholars groaned aloud, even Liu Xiang and Dong Zhongshu struggling to hold their peace.
proposals.reason: 太后 is the empress dowager, a singular titled person, not undifferentiated palace women.

proposals.before: After Han’s revival, Emperor Ming took the throne: he read the sundial’s shadow and staged “The Pure Temple”; spread catalpa shade and let ritual currents shimmer like jade;
proposals.after: After Han’s revival, Emperor Ming took the throne: he read the sundial’s shadow and staged “The Pure Temple”; planted locust-tree shade and opened the jade-ring moat;
proposals.reason: 槐 is the locust/pagoda tree of the academy, not catalpa; 疏璧流 refers to opening the Biyong jade-ring moat, not shimmering ritual currents.

proposals.before: When fiery Han revived and Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he displayed the jade tablet’s shadow and presented “The Pure Temple”; planted catalpa shade and opened out jade-green currents;
proposals.after: When fiery Han revived and Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he displayed the jade tablet’s shadow and presented “The Pure Temple”; planted locust-tree shade and opened out the jade-ring moat;
proposals.reason: Same errors as the idiomatic line: 槐 is not catalpa, and 璧流 is the circular academy moat.

proposals.before: Where there is Yongyon academy music, this is what is meant by “to shift custom and improve morals, nothing surpasses music.”
proposals.after: Where there is Biyong academy music, this is what is meant by “to shift custom and improve morals, nothing surpasses music.”
proposals.reason: 辟雍 is the royal Biyong academy; “Yongyon” is a corrupted transcription, not a source-supported place or institution name.

proposals.before: Jin’s Emperor Wu took Han–Wei patterns as his mold, reviewed precedents from the Simas Jing and Wen, replaced the ritual vessels, yet kept the older musical substance intact.
proposals.after: Jin’s Emperor Wu took Han–Wei patterns as his mold, reviewed precedents left by Emperors Jing and Wen, replaced the ritual vessels, yet kept the older musical substance intact.
proposals.reason: 景文 are the posthumous titles of two emperors, not a fused surname-given pair “Simas Jing” plus a leftover “Wen”.

proposals.before: the ninth year of Taishi saw Minister Xun Xu cast archaic measuring rods to tune intervals, then parade the majestic pieces Zhang Hua’s circle had written beneath the standing pipes.
proposals.after: In the ninth year of Taishi, the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Xun Xu first fashioned ancient foot-rules to tune intervals, then still employed the majestic pieces Zhang Hua’s circle had written, presenting them beneath the standing pipes.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 光祿大夫 and “始作”, and “cast…parade” overstates making rods and presenting the pieces.

proposals.before: Meanwhile Deng Jing and Yin Shang, household advisers, drilled choristers in ritual repertoire; Yin Hu sang suburban and temple hymns; Feng Su and Fu Yang staged archaic dances—every troupe answered to Du Kui.
proposals.after: Meanwhile Deng Jing and Yin Shang, Gentlemen Cavalier Attendants, excelled at drilling ritual music; Yin Hu sang suburban and temple hymns; Feng Su and Fu Yang staged archaic dances—every troupe answered to Du Kui.
proposals.reason: 散騎侍郎 is the court office Gentleman Cavalier Attendant, not a generic household adviser; 善訓雅樂 means they excelled at instructing ritual music, not that they merely drilled choristers.

proposals.before: At the same time Gentlemen for Imperial Household Cadence Deng Jing and Yin Shang excelled at drilling ritual music; singer Yin Hu could perform ancestral-temple and suburban-sacrifice airs; dance masters Feng Su and Fu Yang understood former dynasties’ dances—Du Kui supervised them all.
proposals.after: At the same time Gentlemen Cavalier Attendants Deng Jing and Yin Shang excelled at drilling ritual music; singer Yin Hu could perform ancestral-temple and suburban-sacrifice airs; dance masters Feng Su and Fu Yang understood former dynasties’ dances—Du Kui supervised them all.
proposals.reason: 散騎侍郎 is Gentleman Cavalier Attendant; “Imperial Household Cadence” invents a musical household office the Chinese does not name.

proposals.before: At the outset of Jin’s mandate, institutions existed only in embryo.
proposals.after: At the outset of Emperor Wu’s receiving the mandate, institutions existed only in embryo.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Emperor Wu (武帝) as the person who received the mandate; the idiomatic rendering drops that personal subject and leaves only the polity Jin.

proposals.before: the second year of Taishi ordered suburban and Bright Hall liturgy to borrow Wei forms—echoing Zhou’s habit of calling early rituals Shang-style—while swapping only the hymn lyrics, commissioned from Fu Xuan.
proposals.after: In the second year of Taishi an edict ordered suburban and Bright Hall liturgy to borrow Wei forms—echoing Zhou’s habit of calling early rituals Shang-style—while swapping only the hymn lyrics, commissioned from Fu Xuan.
proposals.reason: The sentence is ungrammatical as published: a year cannot be the agent of 诏; the Chinese subject is an imperial edict in Taishi 2.

proposals.before: King Wen’s pattern glows; his quiet virtue pacifies every quarter.
proposals.after: How King Wen flourished; day by day he pacifies the four quarters.
proposals.reason: 蒸哉 is the Shijing exclamation of flourishing, not a glowing pattern; 日靖四方 is daily pacification of the four quarters.

proposals.before: How Emperor Wen flourished—quieting the four quarters day by day.
proposals.after: How King Wen flourished—quieting the four quarters day by day.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line and the 宣文 / King Wen pairing name King Wen; literal Emperor Wen conflicts with that rendering.

proposals.before: Emperor Wen pairs worthily with Heaven on high.
proposals.after: Emperors Xuan and Wen, as our sovereigns, pair worthily with Heaven on high.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宣文惟後 names the paired Jin ancestral sovereigns Xuan and Wen, not a single Emperor Wen; 惟後 marks them as the ruling house, and 克配彼天 is the matching-Heaven formula.

proposals.before: King Wen alone serves as spouse-partner to High Heaven.
proposals.after: Xuan and Wen are the sovereigns, able to stand as counterparts to that Heaven.
proposals.reason: 宣文 is the Xuan-plus-Wen ancestral pair, not Zhou King Wen; 惟後 is ‘are the sovereigns,’ not ‘alone,’ and 配 is ritual counterpart pairing rather than marital spouse.

proposals.before: Two sage-kings march in accumulated power, doubling that luminous legacy.
proposals.after: The Two Emperors stride in virtue and proclaim this redoubled glory.
proposals.reason: 邁德 means advancing or striding in virtue, not marching in accumulated power; 宣此重光 is broadcasting or proclaiming redoubled radiance, which the literal already captures.

proposals.before: Steaming flesh steams; jade cups lift in toast.
proposals.after: We cook the sacrificial victims; jade cups lift in toast.
proposals.reason: 烹牷牲 is cooking whole sacrificial animals for offering; the current idiomatic line tautologically invents steaming flesh and hides the victims.

proposals.before: When the god draws near—it trails trails of light.
proposals.after: When the god draws near—it trails gleams of light.
proposals.reason: 遺光景 is trailing residual radiance; the literal doubles trails and obscures the light-shadow image.

proposals.before: Supreme Grand glows fierce—sage forebears rise immense.
proposals.after: Radiant is the Grand Supreme—sage ancestors rise immense.
proposals.reason: 太上 is the Grand Supreme ancestor, not the awkward inversion Supreme Grand; 聖祖 is plural sage ancestors in parallel with the rendered English.

proposals.before: Clear shines our martial king—he grandly carries on the line.
proposals.after: Bright is our illustrious deceased father—he grandly carries on the succession.
proposals.reason: 烈考 is the illustrious deceased father (考), not a martial king; 繼序 is ordered succession, which the literal already captures.

proposals.before: Trunk and twigs thrive alike—the base splits open Genesis fortune.
proposals.after: Trunk and branches flourish together—drawing on that beginning, they open primordial fortune.
proposals.reason: 開元 here is ritual diction for opening primal fortune, not the later era name Genesis/Kaiyuan; 資始 means drawing on the origin, not a geological split.

proposals.before: Blazing royal ancestor Xuan—sagely power awe-full and clear.
proposals.after: Blazing royal ancestor Xuan—sagely virtue reverent and bright.
proposals.reason: 聖德欽明 is revered/bright sagely virtue; English awe-full is a corrupted spelling and misreads 欽明.

proposals.before: He picked up Xuan’s thread—aged its achievements firm.
proposals.after: He picked up Xuan’s thread and firmly established that merit.
proposals.reason: 耆定厥功 is the classical idiom for bringing merit to firm completion; idiomatic English misreads 耆 as ‘aged’.

proposals.before: He carried Xuan’s legacy—aged and settled that merit.
proposals.after: He carried Xuan’s legacy—firmly settled that merit.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 耆 as ‘aged’ instead of the established sense ‘bring to completion / settle firmly’.

proposals.before: Bronze tolls shiver—reed banks tune—dance unveils Primordial Opening—chorus launches Eternal Beginning—every deity thrills with joy!
proposals.after: Bells and drums resound—pipes and strings are tuned—they dance Kaiyuan—they sing Yongshi—the gods all rejoice!
proposals.reason: 開元 and 永始 name the dance and song pieces, matching the literal field; Primordial Opening and Eternal Beginning invent glosses and drop the titles.

proposals.before: Young and old alike reverent—above and below observe ritual.
proposals.after: Lesser and greater alike reverent—above and below observe ritual.
proposals.reason: 小大 marks lesser and greater ranks, as in the idiomatic field, not young and old; 鹹 stands for 咸 “all alike.”

proposals.before: Du Kui handed down four classical chamber pieces—“Deer Call,” “Zouyu,” “Cutting Sandalwood,” and “King Wen”—each preserving archaic lyrics and melody.
proposals.after: Du Kui handed down four former elegant-music pieces—“Deer Call,” “Zouyu,” “Cutting Sandalwood,” and “King Wen”—each preserving archaic lyrics and melody.
proposals.reason: 雅樂 denotes court elegant/ritual music, not chamber music; 舊 marks the repertoire as inherited.

proposals.before: Thus at dawn court each New Year, when the commander-in-chief lifts the jade tally and kings of domains bow through ceremony, the classical ensemble housed east of the hall repeats these pieces.
proposals.after: Thus at each New Year’s dawn court, when the Grand Commandant presents the jade disk and regional lords perform the rites, the elegant ensemble of the eastern wing regularly performs these pieces.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not commander-in-chief; 奉璧 is presenting a jade disk, not lifting a tally; 群後 are regional lords.

proposals.before: Later editors swapped the three ceremonial procession poems once more.
proposals.after: Later they again altered the three ceremonial procession poems.
proposals.reason: The verb 改 means the three ritual procession hymns were altered again; “swapped” invents an interchange the Chinese does not state.

proposals.before: the fifth year of Taishi brought a memorial commissioning Fu Xuan, Xun Xu, and Zhang Hua to draft lyrics for New Year ceremonies, royal longevity cups, and feast fanfares.
proposals.after: In the fifth year of Taishi the Secretariat memorialized, commissioning Minister Coachman Fu Xuan, Palace Secretariat Director Xun Xu, and Imperial Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua each to compose hymn texts for New Year ritual processions, princes' longevity toasts, and meal-accompaniment music.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence begins lowercase, omits the three offices named in the Chinese, and reduces 尚書奏 to an impersonal 'brought a memorial' while turning 食舉樂歌詩 into 'feast fanfares.'

proposals.before: So Xun Xu scrapped legacy “Deer Call” text and forged four procession songs foregrounding thrice-yearly court pilgrimage.
proposals.after: So Xun Xu discarded the old “Deer Call” lyrics and composed four procession poems foregrounding the meaning of three-dawn court homage.
proposals.reason: English 'forged' invents fraud; 更作 is composing replacements. 'Thrice-yearly court pilgrimage' also over-specifies 三朝朝宗之義.

proposals.before: The court likewise commissioned Secretariat Vice Director Cheng Gongzhao to supply lyrics.
proposals.after: The court likewise commissioned Secretariat Vice Director Chenggong Sui to supply lyrics.
proposals.reason: Chinese 成公綏 is the compound surname Chenggong plus given name Sui (綏); Gongzhao mismatches 綏.

proposals.before: At the same time an edict also ordered Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Cheng Gongzhao to compose texts.
proposals.after: At the same time an edict also ordered Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Chenggong Sui to compose texts.
proposals.reason: Chinese 成公綏 is Chenggong Sui, not Gongzhao; 綏 is Sui.

proposals.before: Grand Dawn Levee Processional—Cheng Gongzhao
proposals.after: Grand Dawn Levee Processional—Chenggong Sui
proposals.reason: Attribution 成公綏 should be romanized Chenggong Sui, not Cheng Gongzhao.

proposals.before: Processional Song for the Great New Year Assembly—by Cheng Gongzhao
proposals.after: Processional Song for the Great New Year Assembly—by Chenggong Sui
proposals.reason: Attribution 成公綏 should be romanized Chenggong Sui, not Cheng Gongzhao.

proposals.before: Grave and luminous the sky son—his radiance spans every kingdom.
proposals.after: Grave and luminous the Son of Heaven—his radiance spans every kingdom.
proposals.reason: 天子 is the standard title Son of Heaven; sky son obscures the office being named.

proposals.before: Plumed standards glare at zenith seat—bronze storms shake empyrean peace.
proposals.after: Plumed standards glare at zenith seat—bells and drums shake empyrean peace.
proposals.reason: 鐘鼓 means bells and drums; bronze storms invents a metaphor not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Hoary brows hymn holy sovereign—auspicious blessing refreshes each dawn.
proposals.after: May longevity bless the holy sovereign—auspicious blessing refreshes each dawn.
proposals.reason: 眉壽祚聖皇 is a longevity blessing on the sage emperor, not hoary brows hymning him.

proposals.before: Mandate answered its hour—sacred power passed—four reigns stacked glory anew.
proposals.after: Mandate answered its hour—sacred power passed—four generations stacked glory anew.
proposals.reason: Chinese 四世 means four generations (shi), not four reigns; the hymn’s imperial sequence is generational.

proposals.before: Receiving mandate matching its season—handed sacred virtue—four reigns doubled radiance.
proposals.after: Receiving mandate matching its season—handed sacred virtue—four generations doubled radiance.
proposals.reason: Literal 世 is generation; rendering it as reigns misstates the kinship-temporal claim.

proposals.before: Three reigns layer doubled gleam—Taishi splits primordial cornerstone.
proposals.after: Three reigns layer doubled gleam—Taishi opens the grand foundation.
proposals.reason: 開洪基 means opening a vast dynastic foundation; splits primordial cornerstone invents a rupture and mistranslates 開 and 洪基.

proposals.before: They succor folk and nurture creatures—modeling Potter Gong’s even kiln.
proposals.after: They succor folk and nurture creatures—modeling the potter’s even wheel.
proposals.reason: 陶均 is the potter’s wheel used as a cosmic metaphor; Potter Gong invents a personal name and kiln misreads 均.

proposals.before: They order four quarters—they polish sun, moon, stars.
proposals.after: They order four seasons—they polish sun, moon, stars.
proposals.reason: 序四時 means sequencing the four seasons, not the four quarters; the idiomatic line mistranslates 四時 as spatial quarters while the literal already has seasons.

proposals.before: Bright dynastic founder—supporting eras, steadying hours.
proposals.after: Radiant illustrious ancestor—supporting eras, steadying hours.
proposals.reason: 皇皇顯祖 is the illustrious royal ancestor, not a dynastic founder; founding language belongs to later 烈考 lines (肇建帝業，開國有晉).

proposals.before: Heaven and Earth already eased—nine provinces lie squared.
proposals.after: The cosmos already at peace—nine provinces lie squared.
proposals.reason: 宇宙 means the cosmos or universe, not the pair Heaven and Earth.

proposals.before: Royal Toast Anthem for Dawn Court—Xun Xu
proposals.after: Longevity Toast Song for the Great New Year Assembly of Princes and Dukes—Xun Xu
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 正旦大會 and 王公上壽酒, rendering a generic dawn-court anthem instead of the New Year assembly longevity toast of princes and dukes.

proposals.before: Long live our sovereign—towering as Song summit.
proposals.after: Our emperor is long-lived and lofty; our emperor is flourishing as the Song peak.
proposals.reason: The source is two parallel 我皇 clauses (壽而隆 / 茂而嵩); the idiomatic line collapses them and attaches only the Song-peak image to a single toast.

proposals.before: Wen and Wu powers blossomed—thick achievement stacked glory.
proposals.after: Civil and martial powers blossomed—thick achievement stacked glory.
proposals.reason: 文武 here is the paired civil/martial virtues of the former emperor, not the personal names Wen and Wu; surfaces still follow the packet text.

proposals.before: Dragon flight marks revolution—his glare scorches eight wastes.
proposals.after: Dragon flight marks revolution—his covering warmth reaches the eight wastes.
proposals.reason: 燾 means covering/overshadowing warmth of rule, not scorching glare; 臨燾八荒 is the sage-king’s protective reach over the eight wilds.

proposals.before: Dragon soaring shifting mandate—his brilliance broils eight wilds.
proposals.after: Dragon soaring shifting mandate—his brilliance covers the eight wilds.
proposals.reason: 燾 is cover/shelter, not broil; the line describes radiance covering the eight wilds.

proposals.before: Long ago King Xuan—numinous terror calmed outer shores.
proposals.after: Long ago our ancestor Xuan—numinous terror calmed outer shores.
proposals.reason: 祖宣 is the ancestral temple-name Xuan, not a king; the idiomatic line invents King and drops ancestor.

proposals.before: People of Han and Hu lands brought ensembles—court pitches rang balanced tubes.
proposals.after: People of Han and Ye brought ensembles—court pitches rang balanced tubes.
proposals.reason: 韓濊 names the Han and Ye (濊) peoples, not Hu (胡).

proposals.before: Han and Hu peoples advanced music—palace modes tuned clear even scales.
proposals.after: Han and Ye peoples advanced music—palace modes tuned clear even scales.
proposals.reason: 韓濊 names the Han and Ye (濊) peoples, not Hu (胡).

proposals.before: We hold aging ceremonies—thereby banqueting full bureaucracy.
proposals.after: We hold longevity rites—thereby banqueting the full bureaucracy.
proposals.reason: 壽禮 are longevity/birthday-tribute rites, not ceremonies of aging; the idiomatic rendering inverts the honorific sense of 壽.

proposals.before: Twin glory of Shun exalted the royal path—martial margins sometimes spurned allegiance.
proposals.after: Chonghua exalted the imperial Way—martial margins sometimes spurned allegiance.
proposals.reason: 重華 is Shun’s personal name Chonghua, not a descriptive phrase “twin glory of Shun.” The line names the sage-ruler as the one who raised the imperial Way.

proposals.before: Shun’s doubled splendor raised imperial Way—warlike tribes sometimes refused guesthood.
proposals.after: Chonghua raised the imperial Way—warlike tribes sometimes refused guesthood.
proposals.reason: 重華 is the personal name, not “Shun’s doubled splendor.” Render the name rather than etymologizing 重 and 華 as a possessive metaphor.

proposals.before: Border wolves renounced celestial duty—stirred chaos round the capital belt.
proposals.after: The Xianyun renounced celestial duty—stirred chaos round the capital belt.
proposals.reason: Chinese 玁犬允 is the ethnonym Xianyun (玁狁), not generic wolves; the idiomatic line erases the named people-group.

proposals.before: Battle cars shake frontier north—legions of generals magnify royal terror.
proposals.after: Battle cars shake frontier north—legions of generals magnify imperial majesty.
proposals.reason: 皇威 is imperial majesty or awe, not terror; the current rendering inverts the praise of royal prestige.

proposals.before: Royal heroines draped dynastic standard—“Greater Ya” hymns three brides.
proposals.after: Huang and Ying draped dynastic standard—“Greater Ya” hymns three consorts.
proposals.reason: 皇英 are the named legendary consorts Huang and Ying; 三妃 are consorts, not brides, and the idiomatic line drops both identifications.

proposals.before: Joint and marrow parted yet kin—how could cousins count as strangers?
proposals.after: Joint and marrow parted yet kin—how could brothers count as strangers?
proposals.reason: 昆弟 means brothers, not cousins; the literal line already has brothers.

proposals.before: Trunk and twigs taste joint joy—“Pear Blossom” ode recalls ancestors.
proposals.after: Trunk and twigs taste joint joy—“Cherry-flower” (Tangdi) ode recalls ancestors.
proposals.reason: 棠棣 is the Shijing Tangdi (cherry-flower / brothers) ode, not a pear-blossom poem.

proposals.before: Root and branches share deep gladness—“Pear Tree” hymn marks ancient folk.
proposals.after: Root and branches share deep gladness—“Cherry-flower” hymn marks ancient folk.
proposals.reason: 棠棣 is not a pear tree; the poem title is Tangdi (cherry-flower).

proposals.before: Finished scales were promulgated to the Ministry of Rites for adoption by court music bureaus.
proposals.after: Once the pitch-pipes were complete, they were promulgated to the Chamberlain of Ceremonial for Grand Music, General Regulation, Drum-and-Bugle, and Pure Shop to adopt them.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits the four named music offices 太樂、總章、鼓吹、清商 that the Chinese lists as the adopters under 太常.

proposals.before: Xun Xu cut twelve fresh panpipes to tune classical pitch for state halls; he insisted modes aligned, though critics sneered his ear was blunt.
proposals.after: Xun Xu cut twelve fresh pitch-flutes to tune classical pitch for state halls; he insisted modes aligned, though critics sneered his ear was blunt.
proposals.reason: 律笛 are pitch-flutes, not panpipes; the idiomatic rendering invents the wrong instrument class.

proposals.before: Each court feast, Xun heard sabotage in Ruan’s silence—read it mutiny—and banished him as Shiping prefect.
proposals.after: Whenever music was performed at public gatherings, Xun took Ruan to be judging it out of tune, regarded him as a rival, and posted him out as chancellor of Shiping.
proposals.reason: The Chinese says Xun understood Ruan to call the music 不調 (out of tune), not that Xun heard sabotage in silence; 出…為始平相 is posting as Shiping chancellor, not a mutiny narrative.

proposals.before: Later peasants dug up a Zhou jade yardstick; against it Xu’s orchestra proved uniformly short one chi—then he bowed to Ruan’s finesse and summoned him home.
proposals.after: Later a farmer tilling in the wilds found a Zhou-period jade foot-rule; measured against it, Xu’s bells, drums, and metal, stone, silk, and bamboo instruments were all short by one grain—then he conceded Ruan’s subtlety and summoned him back.
proposals.reason: 短校一米 is a millet/rice grain (米), not a chi (尺); 田父 is a singular farmer, and the comparison is to the instruments Xu had tuned.

proposals.before: Later a farmer tilling wild fields unearthed a Zhou-period jade foot-rule; Xu compared it to bells, drums, metal, stone, silk, and bamboo he had tuned—all proved one chi shorter than his calibration—thus he conceded Xian’s subtlety and recalled him.
proposals.after: Later a farmer tilling wild fields unearthed a Zhou-period jade foot-rule; Xu compared it to bells, drums, metal, stone, silk, and bamboo he had tuned—all proved one grain shorter than his calibration—thus he conceded Xian’s subtlety and recalled him.
proposals.reason: 一米 is a grain, not 一尺 (one chi).

proposals.before: Those folk loved war dance; the founding emperor savored its savage edge, watched often, then told court artists to master it.
proposals.after: Those folk loved dance; the founding emperor savored its savage edge, watched often, then told court musicians to master it.
proposals.reason: 喜舞 is delight in dance, not specifically a war dance; 樂人 are musicians, not court artists.

proposals.before: The Yu River runs through Langzhong; settlers lent their name to what courtiers called the Bayu drill.
proposals.after: Langzhong has the Yu River; because they dwelled there, it was named the Bayu Dance.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names the dance from residence by the Yu in Langzhong; it does not mention settlers lending a name, courtiers, or a drill.

proposals.before: Early Wei charged Libationer Wang Can with drafting fresh words.
proposals.after: Early Wei charged Army Counsel Libationer Wang Can with drafting fresh words.
proposals.reason: 軍謀祭酒 is the Army Counsel Libationer office; rendering only Libationer drops 軍謀.

proposals.before: Jingchu 1 brought a memorial comparing Shang-Zhou-Han survivals; weighing deeds against virtue, ministers debuted Martial Inception, All-pervading Dawn, and Pattern Splendor—each dancer clutching plumes and pitch-pipes.
proposals.after: Jingchu 1 brought a memorial reviewing remnant ritual tunes of the Three Dynasties; weighing deeds against virtue, ministers debuted Martial Inception, All-pervading Dawn, and Pattern Splendor—each dancer clutching plumes and pitch-pipes.
proposals.reason: 三代 means the Three Dynasties (classically Xia, Shang, and Zhou), not Shang-Zhou-Han; the idiomatic line invents Han and drops the ritual-music sense of 禮樂遺曲.

decisions.reason: The source 人能弘道 is a gnomic Analects line marked by 能 (capacity) and present-tense 非道弘人; the published past tense “broadened / it was never” turns a standing maxim into a completed historical event. The replacement restores that modal sense in natural English.
堯作《咸池》 names Yao’s ritual piece Xianchi. “Mulberry Pool” would require 桑 and is an invented title.
The same source title 《咸池》 is Xianchi; the literal “Mulberry Pool” invents 桑 and mistranslates the music name.
平王逢亂 says King Ping encountered disorder, not that “his reign dissolved.” The original adds an unsupported collapse of the reign itself.
其周德之衰乎 is a rhetorical question marked by 乎, which the following concessive 猶有先王之遺風焉 presupposes. Rendering it as the flat assertion “This is Zhou virtue in decay” drops that interrogative mood.
太后 is a singular titled empress dowager, not undifferentiated “palace women.”
槐 is the locust/pagoda tree of the academy, not catalpa, and 疏璧流 is opening the Biyong jade-ring moat, not shimmering ritual currents.
The literal line repeats both errors: 槐 is not catalpa, and 璧流 is the circular academy moat.
辟雍 is the royal Biyong academy; “Yongyon” is a corrupted transcription with no source support.
景文 are the posthumous titles of Emperors Jing and Wen. “Simas Jing and Wen” wrongly fuses a surname onto 景 as if it were a given name.
The source names 光祿大夫, 始作古尺, 仍以…高文, and 陳諸下管. The original drops the office and 始作, and “cast…parade” overstates making the foot-rule and presenting the pieces.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 光祿大夫荀勖始作古尺，以調聲韻，仍以張華等所制高文，陳諸下管

decisions.reason: 散騎侍郎 is the office Gentleman Cavalier Attendant, not a generic household adviser, and 善訓雅樂 means they excelled at instructing ritual music, not that they merely drilled choristers.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 散騎侍郎鄧靜、尹商善訓雅樂

decisions.reason: 散騎侍郎 is Gentleman Cavalier Attendant. “Imperial Household Cadence” invents a musical household office the Chinese does not name.
武帝受命之初 names Emperor Wu as the person who received the mandate; “Jin’s mandate” drops that personal subject.
泰始二年，詔… has an imperial edict as the agent. The published line is ungrammatical and makes the year itself issue the order.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 泰始二年，詔郊祀明堂禮樂權用魏儀

decisions.after: How Xuan and Wen flourished; day by day they pacify the four quarters.
decisions.reason: 蒸哉 and 日靖四方 are correctly restored, but 宣文 in this Jin suburban hymn is the ancestral pair Xuan and Wen, not Zhou King Wen. The same chapter’s later 宣文惟後 confirms that pairing.

decisions.after: How Xuan and Wen flourished—quieting the four quarters day by day.
decisions.reason: There is a real naming error, but replacing “Emperor Wen” with “King Wen” is still wrong. 宣文 is the Jin ancestral pair Xuan and Wen, not a single Zhou or Jin “King/Emperor Wen.”
宣文惟後 names the paired Jin ancestral sovereigns Xuan and Wen as 後; 克配彼天 is the matching-Heaven formula. The original collapses the pair into a single Emperor Wen.
宣文 is the Xuan-plus-Wen pair, not Zhou King Wen; 惟後 marks them as sovereigns rather than “alone,” and 配 is ritual counterpart pairing, not a marital spouse.
邁德 is advancing/striding in virtue, not marching in accumulated power, and 宣此重光 is proclaiming redoubled radiance.
烹牷牲 is cooking whole sacrificial victims for offering. “Steaming flesh steams” is tautological and hides the victims.
遺光景 is trailing residual radiance. The literal “trails trails of light” is a doubled-word error that obscures 光景.
太上 is the Grand Supreme ancestor, not the inverted “Supreme Grand,” and 赫赫 is radiance rather than an awkward “glows fierce.”
烈考 is the illustrious deceased father (考), not a martial king, and 繼序 is ordered succession.
資始開元 is drawing on the origin to open primal fortune. “Splits open Genesis fortune” invents a geological rupture and anachronistically reads 開元 as the later era name.
聖德欽明 is sagely virtue revered and bright. “Awe-full” is a corrupted spelling and misreads 欽明 as mere awe, while “power” is not 德.
耆定厥功 is the classical idiom for bringing merit to firm completion, not “aging” achievements.
The literal likewise misreads 耆 as “aged” instead of firmly settling/completing the merit.
舞開元，歌永始 names the dance and song pieces, parallel to the following 舞象德，歌詠功. “Primordial Opening” and “Eternal Beginning” invent glosses and drop the titles.
小大 marks lesser and greater ranks, as the idiomatic line already has, not young and old; 鹹 stands for 咸.
舊雅樂 is inherited court elegant/ritual music, not “classical chamber pieces.”
太尉 is Grand Commandant, 奉璧 is presenting a jade disk, and 群後 are regional lords. The original’s commander-in-chief, tally, and “kings of domains” are unsupported.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太尉奉璧，群後行禮，東廂雅樂常作者是也

decisions.reason: 後又改三篇之行禮詩 means the three ritual procession hymns were altered again. “Swapped” invents an interchange, and “editors” is not in the Chinese.
尚書奏 commissions 太僕傅玄、中書監荀勖、黃門侍郎張華 to write 正旦行禮 and 王公上壽酒、食舉樂歌詩. The original begins lowercase, drops the three offices, and turns meal-accompaniment hymns into “feast fanfares.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尚書奏，使太僕傅玄、中書監荀勖、黃門侍郎張華各造正旦行禮及王公上壽酒、食舉樂歌詩

decisions.reason: 更作 is composing replacements, not “forging,” and 三朝朝宗之義 is the meaning of three-dawn court homage, not a thrice-yearly pilgrimage.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 除《鹿鳴》舊歌更作行禮詩四篇，先陳三朝朝宗之義

decisions.reason: 成公綏 is the compound surname Chenggong plus given name Sui (綏). Gongzhao mismatches 綏.
The literal likewise mis-romanizes 成公綏 as Cheng Gongzhao; 綏 is Sui.
The heading attribution 成公綏 should be Chenggong Sui, not Cheng Gongzhao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 正旦大會行禮歌成公綏

decisions.reason: The literal heading likewise misnames 成公綏 as Cheng Gongzhao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 正旦大會行禮歌成公綏

decisions.reason: 天子 is the title Son of Heaven. “Sky son” obscures the office being named.
鐘鼓 means bells and drums. “Bronze storms” invents a metaphor not in the Chinese.
眉壽祚聖皇 is a longevity blessing on the sage emperor, not hoary brows hymning him.
四世重光 is four generations of stacked radiance, not four reigns.
Literal 世 is generation; rendering it as reigns misstates the kinship-temporal claim.

decisions.after: Three generations layer doubled gleam—Taishi opens the grand foundation.
decisions.reason: 開洪基 is correctly “opens the grand foundation,” not a split cornerstone, but 三葉 is three generations/leaves of the house, not “three reigns.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三葉合重光，泰始開洪基。

decisions.reason: 陶均 is the potter’s wheel as a cosmic metaphor. “Potter Gong” invents a personal name and “kiln” misreads 均.
序四時 is sequencing the four seasons, not spatial quarters.
皇皇顯祖 is the illustrious royal ancestor, not a dynastic founder; founding language belongs to later 烈考 lines.
宇宙 means the cosmos, not the pair Heaven and Earth.
正旦大會王公上壽酒歌 names a New Year assembly longevity toast of princes and dukes. “Royal Toast Anthem for Dawn Court” drops 正旦大會 and 王公上壽酒.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 正旦大會王公上壽酒歌荀勖

decisions.reason: The source is two parallel 我皇 clauses (壽而隆 / 茂而嵩). Collapsing them into a single “Long live… towering as Song summit” drops one clause and attaches the Song-peak image to the wrong half.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 我皇壽而隆，我皇茂而嵩。

decisions.reason: 文武發揮 is the former emperor’s paired civil and martial virtues, not the personal names Wen and Wu.
臨燾八荒 is protective covering/overshadowing warmth over the eight wilds, not a scorching glare.
燾 is cover/shelter, not broil. The line describes radiance covering the eight wilds.
往我祖宣 names ancestral temple-name Xuan. “King Xuan” invents a kingship title and drops 祖.
韓濊 names the Han and Ye (濊) peoples, not Hu (胡).
The literal likewise misreads 濊 as Hu. The source ethnonym is Ye.
壽禮 are longevity/birthday-tribute rites, not ceremonies of aging. The original inverts the honorific sense of 壽.
重華 is Shun’s personal name Chonghua, not a descriptive “twin glory of Shun.” The line names that sage-ruler as the one who raised the imperial Way.
重華 should be rendered as the personal name Chonghua, not etymologized as “Shun’s doubled splendor.”
玁犬允 is the ethnonym Xianyun (玁狁), not generic “border wolves.” The original erases the named people.
皇威 is imperial majesty or awe, not terror. The original inverts the praise of royal prestige.
皇英 are the named legendary consorts Huang and Ying, and 三妃 are consorts, not brides. “Royal heroines” and “three brides” drop both identifications.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皇英垂帝典，《大雅》詠三妃。

decisions.reason: 昆弟 means brothers, not cousins.
《棠棣》 is the Shijing Tangdi (cherry-flower / brothers) ode, not a pear-blossom poem.
棠棣 is not a pear tree; the poem title is Tangdi (cherry-flower).
律成，遂班下太常，使太樂、總章、鼓吹、清商施用 names four music offices under the Chamberlain of Ceremonial. “Ministry of Rites… court music bureaus” omits those offices.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 班下太常，使太樂、總章、鼓吹、清商施用

decisions.reason: 律笛 are pitch-flutes, not panpipes.

勖意咸謂之不調 means Xun took Ruan to be judging the music out of tune, 以為異己 regarded him as a rival, and 出咸為始平相 posted him as chancellor of Shiping. Sabotage, silence, mutiny, banishment, and “prefect” are all unsupported.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 每公會樂作，勖意咸謂之不調，以為異己，乃出咸為始平相。

decisions.reason: 田父 is a singular farmer, 玉尺 a jade foot-rule, and 短校一米 a discrepancy of one grain (米), not one chi. The original also invents a plural peasantry and an undifferentiated “orchestra.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 田父耕于野，得周時玉尺……皆短校一米

decisions.reason: 一米 is a grain, not 一尺. The literal’s “one chi” is a unit error.
喜舞 is delight in dance, not specifically a war dance, and 樂人 are musicians, not court artists.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其俗喜舞……後使樂人習之

decisions.reason: 閬中有渝水，因其所居，故名曰《巴渝舞》 names the dance from residence by the Yu in Langzhong. Settlers lending a name, courtiers, and a “drill” are invented.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 閬中有渝水，因其所居，故名曰《巴渝舞》。

decisions.reason: 軍謀祭酒 is the Army Counsel Libationer office; rendering only “Libationer” drops 軍謀.
三代禮樂遺曲 are remnant ritual-music tunes of the Three Dynasties (classically Xia, Shang, and Zhou), not Shang-Zhou-Han survivals.

claimRetractions.reason: The title “King Wen” for 文 in 宣文惟後 was created by the literal “King Wen alone.” The source honors Jin Emperor Wen as one of the Xuan-and-Wen pair, already captured by the Emperor Wen title claim.
祖宣 is ancestral temple-name Xuan, not the title King Xuan. That kingship title was created solely by the bad idiomatic rendering.

claimRevisions.reason: The restored title of 咸池 is Xianchi; “Mulberry Pool” existed only in the mistranslation.
Yao’s composition remains 咸池; only the English work name must change from the invented “Mulberry Pool” to Xianchi.
成公綏 is Chenggong Sui; the extracted English personal name Cheng Gongzhao was created by misreading 綏 as Zhao.
